query: For initially solid FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles exposed to the premelting and melting regime, the limited understanding of their thermal response prevents clear definition of their usable temperature range and behavior during high-temperature synthesis. What single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs the onset and progression of their phase transition and why? Specify a controlled comparison, predicted observations relative to the starting baseline, relevant boundary conditions, supporting evidence from prior nanoparticle studies, and a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The onset and progression of premelting and melting in FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles is governed by preferential surface segregation of Cu to form a lower-melting, liquid-like nanoshell, which nucleates at the surface around ~0.8 T_m (bulk) and thickens inward with increasing temperature.
generation.material_initial_state: Solid, single-phase face-centered-cubic FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles (5–10 nm diameter) with uniform bulk composition at room temperature
generation.intervention: Heating from room temperature up to and beyond the bulk melting temperature (T_m ≈1600 K) under inert argon at 10 K/min
generation.conditions: Nanoparticle diameter 5–10 nm; argon atmosphere, 1 atm; heating rate 10 K/min; no oxide shell or external fields
generation.mechanism: Upon heating, Cu atoms diffuse and segregate to the nanoparticle surface, locally reducing the melting point and creating a disordered, mobile surface layer at ~0.8 T_m. As temperature increases this layer grows in thickness, eventually causing complete core melting.
generation.predicted_outcome: In situ TEM/EDS will reveal a ~1–2 atomic‐layer disordered, Cu-rich shell at ≈0.8 T_m, increasing to ~1–2 nm by ≈0.9 T_m. DSC will show an onset of melting ≈100 K below the bulk T_m for Cu-containing NPs, whereas Cu‐free FeNiCrCo NPs will melt closer to the bulk T_m without observable premelting.
generation.baseline: Uniform crystalline FeNiCrCoCu NPs at room temperature showing no surface disorder
generation.boundary: Applies to 5–10 nm NPs heated ≤10 K/min in inert atmosphere; outside these size or heating‐rate ranges behavior may differ
generation.uncertainty: Exact onset temperature and shell‐thickness evolution depend on size dispersion and heating rate; quantitative values approximate

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two samples: FeNiCrCoCu and Cu‐free FeNiCrCo HEA nanoparticles (5–10 nm). Heat both under identical inert‐argon conditions at 10 K/min. Use in situ TEM with EDS to monitor surface structure/composition at incremental temperatures and DSC to record melting‐onset temperatures.
measurements: In situ TEM imaging of surface crystallinity
EDS mapping of surface vs core composition
Measurement of premelted layer thickness by TEM
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If FeNiCrCoCu NPs do not show early surface disorder or Cu enrichment prior to bulk melting, or if FeNiCrCo NPs exhibit similar surface‐premelting features and melting‐onset temperatures, then the hypothesis is falsified.
